Al-Watan Bank Files for Bankruptcy Amidst Mounting Losses in Saudi Arabia

Al-Watan Bank, a mid-sized Saudi Arabian banking institution, has filed for bankruptcy, sending ripples through the Kingdom’s banking sector as it moves to protect its assets and assess future options. The Riyadh-based lender, established in 1986, announced the court filing late Monday, citing persistent liquidity challenges and a sharp increase in non-performing loans over the past two years.

At the time of writing, Al-Watan Bank’s operations have been significantly curtailed. Branches across Saudi Arabia remain open for basic inquiries, but lending activities have been suspended, and customers are unable to access new credit lines or renew existing facilities. The bank’s digital platforms are functioning for account monitoring and limited transactions, though several services are reportedly experiencing delays.

“The Board has made the difficult decision to initiate bankruptcy proceedings in order to ensure an orderly process for all stakeholders,” said Saeed Al-Mutairi, Chairman of Al-Watan Bank, in an official statement. “Our priority remains the protection of depositor interests and maintaining transparency throughout this process.”

The Saudi Arabian Monetary Authority (SAMA) has confirmed it is closely monitoring developments and working with the bank’s appointed administrators to oversee the proceedings. According to industry analysts, Al-Watan Bank’s difficulties underscore broader sectoral challenges stemming from sluggish credit growth and heightened regulatory scrutiny.

The Saudi Banking Association expressed concern for employees and clients, noting that support measures are being discussed. The bankruptcy process is ongoing, with further updates expected as the situation develops.
